title: Usage Registry Explorer & Export Orchestrator for Token-level Cost Attribution
creator: Claire Huang
description:
Problem: Customers operating LLM features (chat, embeddings, batch generation) need a trustworthy way to reconcile token-level cost by conversation, route, and business entity. Current cost panels surface aggregates but lack traceable line items, role-aware exports, and a compact preview for large workloads.

Goal: Design an 'Usage Registry Explorer' within Redwood Console that: (1) surfaces token-level cost decomposition across message boundaries; (2) maps spend to attribution dimensions (project, route, user, model-variant); (3) provides flexible export orchestration (sampled CSVs, compressed parquet, ledger bundles) with role-aware previews and masking for PHI; (4) integrates with rollouts to show cost delta by canary cohort.

High-level UX: A three-column workspace: left = filters & saved queries; center = a paginated ledger view (one line per message or prompt invocation) with expandable context showing KV cache hits, batching group, token counts, model variant, and effective unit rate; right = attribution panel with stacked attribution waterfall (route -> user -> model -> quantization). Key interactions: inline sampling toggle (sample 1/10/100 rows), export composer modal (choose fields, anonymization rules, compression), and cohort compare overlay (compare two time windows or rollout groups).

Design constraints & principles: prioritize readability at scale (virtualized rows), preserve auditability (each ledger line links to an immutable request-id and optional trace link), support privacy controls (PII masking, column redaction), and keep exports deterministic (stable sorting and sampling seeds for reproducible samples). Performance targets: initial render < 600ms for 500 rows, streaming load for full result sets, and export orchestration that pages through backend cursor without blocking UI.

Deliverables: interactive Figma prototype (filter flows, export composer, cohort overlay), acceptance criteria, annotated handoff tokens for engineering (data contract + example CSV/Parquet), and a short research brief with customer interview highlights and edge cases.
acceptance_criteria: Ledger view renders with virtualized rows and column toggles; each row shows timestamp, request-id, token_in, token_out, model_variant, route, and cost_estimate
Expandable row reveals request metadata: prompt hash, KV cache hit status, batch id, and link to tracing dashboard
Attribution panel correctly aggregates spend by selected dimension and shows top-10 contributors with percent share
Export composer supports CSV/Parquet, field selection, anonymization rules, compression, and generates a backend job link with status
Sampling controls provide deterministic samples (seeded) and a sample-preview before export
Cohort compare overlay shows cost delta, normalized per-req TPS, and highlights statistical significance for top contributors
Design assets (Figma prototype) include responsive layouts for wide desktop and small laptop screens
Privacy controls allow column redaction and require role permission to include user identifiers in exports
Design handoff includes data contract example files and a small contract test dataset for engineering
